literal: To those who perform deeds, not shunning and rejecting forbidden deeds, those deeds themselves, even if they succeed, will bring distress.
translation: To those who perform actions without shunning what has been forbidden, those very deeds, even if successfully completed, will only bring ruin.
modern: விலக்கப்பட்ட செயல்களை விலக்கித் தவிர்க்காமல் செய்தவர்களுக்கு, அச்செயல்கள் வெற்றிகரமாக முடிந்தாலும் துன்பத்தையே தரும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of maintaining purity of action by avoiding forbidden deeds. The repetition of the root 'kaṭi' in 'kaṭinta' and 'kaṭintu' underscores the absolute necessity of shunning unethical actions. The poet warns that even if such forbidden acts are successfully completed and seem to yield results, they will ultimately bring only misery ('pīḻai') to the doer. True success cannot be built on a foundation of forbidden deeds, as the consequences of the action itself will eventually lead to ruin.
